issues.legal_issue: A coparcener cannot maintain a suit for a permanent injunction that prevents a family manager from alienating coparcenary property, where the coparcener can challenge the completed alienation and seek recovery of the property.
material_facts: The sons claimed that the house was ancestral coparcenary property and that the proposed sale was neither for legal necessity nor for the benefit of the family estate.
The family manager had agreed to sell the house, and the sons sought a permanent injunction preventing him from selling or alienating it to the proposed purchaser or anyone else.
The sons had an available remedy to challenge the alienation and seek recovery of the property after the sale was completed.
The injunction sought would have barred alienation even if a genuine legal necessity or benefit to the estate later justified a sale.
issues.conclusion: The suit for a permanent injunction restraining the family manager from alienating the coparcenary property was not maintainable, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Mitakshara Hindu law, a coparcener has an interest by birth but cannot interfere with the manager’s acts of management; the manager may alienate joint family property for legal necessity, benefit of the estate, or to meet an antecedent debt. A coparcener may challenge an unjustified completed alienation, but has no corresponding right to obstruct a proposed alienation. Sections 37 and 38 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 govern perpetual injunctions, and section 41(h) bars an injunction where an equally efficacious remedy is available by another usual mode of proceeding. The Court relied on Hunoomanpersaud Pandey v. Mussumat Babooee Munraj Koonweree and Jujhar Singh v. Giani Talok Singh, and distinguished the contrary view in Shiv Kumar Mool Chand Arora v. Mool Chand Jaswant Singh.

predicates.coparcener_seeks_permanent_injunction: A coparcener brings a suit seeking a permanent injunction against the family manager.
predicates.seeks_to_block_manager_alienation: The coparcener seeks to prevent the manager from alienating family property before the alienation is completed.
predicates.post_alienation_challenge_and_recovery_a: The coparcener can challenge a completed alienation and seek recovery of the property through another proceeding.

issues.definition: When a coparcener seeks a permanent injunction to stop a family manager’s proposed alienation and can challenge the completed alienation and seek recovery, the coparcener cannot maintain the suit to block the alienation.

issues.legal_issue: A suit framed as one for permanent injunction cannot determine whether disputed property is ancestral coparcenary property or the manager’s self-acquired property as a basis for granting relief.
material_facts: The manager’s agreement described the house as his self-acquired property.
The sons claimed that the house was ancestral property in which they had coparcenary interests.
The suit was framed as one for permanent injunction against alienation, and ownership classification was disputed.
issues.conclusion: The disputed question whether the property was self-acquired or ancestral had to be decided before relief could be granted, but it could not be determined in the suit as framed for permanent injunction.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the character of the property must be determined before relief dependent on coparcenary rights can be granted, and that this determination could not be made in the suit as framed for permanent injunction. This point was applied alongside the Court’s ruling under sections 38 and 41(h) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 that the requested injunction was unavailable where an efficacious alternative remedy existed.

predicates.permanent_injunction_suit: A party brings a suit framed as a claim for permanent injunctive relief.
predicates.property_character_is_disputed: The parties dispute whether the property belongs to the family jointly or is the manager’s separate property.
predicates.requested_relief_depends_on_property_cha: The requested relief depends on establishing the property’s character.

issues.definition: If a permanent-injunction suit involves disputed property character and the requested relief depends on that character, the character cannot be decided in the suit as framed.

issues.legal_issue: An injunction may be granted against a family manager in a coparcener’s case based on waste or ouster, but not as a blanket restraint on alienation.
material_facts: The sons sought a broad injunction preventing the manager from selling or alienating the house to the proposed purchaser or any other person.
The Court stated that an injunction may be available to a coparcener in a case of waste or ouster, while the suit before it sought a blanket restraint on alienation.
issues.conclusion: An injunction may be granted against a family manager at a coparcener’s instance in a case of waste or ouster, but a blanket permanent injunction barring alienation, including alienation for legal necessity, cannot be granted.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished a specific injunction addressing waste or ouster from a blanket prohibition on alienation. A manager has power to alienate family property for legally recognized family purposes, while the Specific Relief Act’s provisions governing injunctions do not support a blanket restraint that prevents even a justified alienation. The Court discussed sections 37, 38 and 41 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, and relied on the Mitakshara principles described in Hunoomanpersaud Pandey v. Mussumat Babooee Munraj Koonweree.

predicates.coparcener_seeks_injunction_against_fami: A coparcener seeks an injunction against the manager of family property.
predicates.manager_commits_waste: The manager commits waste affecting family property.
predicates.manager_ousts_coparcener: The manager ousts the coparcener from the relevant property or enjoyment of it.

issues.definition: When a coparcener seeks an injunction against a family manager and the manager commits waste or ousts the coparcener, the court may grant an injunction addressing that conduct.
